card.title: Ch 01 · Paine's two words: cite the section
card.job: The paragraph shows Paine separating society from government; the quotation needs its section named.
card.before: Thomas Paine's pamphlet *Common Sense* reached its readers in 1776, and the edition printed by W. and T. Bradford in Philadelphia is dated February 14, 1776.[^paine_edition]
card.after: He gave each word its own origin: "Society is produced by our wants, and government by our wickedness."[^paine_wants]

current.text: Paine opened his argument by pulling apart two words his readers used as one: "Society in every state is a blessing, but government even in its best state is but a necessary evil; in its worst state an intolerable one." The sentence carries the whole pamphlet's frame.

card.title: Ch 02 · Hamilton wrote "reflection and choice"
card.job: The paragraph quotes Hamilton's statement of the question the ratification debate puts to the people.
card.before: Alexander Hamilton addressed the first *Federalist* paper "To the People of the State of New York," and the Project Gutenberg text heads it "For the Independent Journal."[^fed1_heading]

current.text: Hamilton framed the ratification debate as a test: whether "societies of men are really capable or not of establishing good government from reflection and design, or whether they are forever destined to depend for their political constitutions on accident and force."[^fed1_test]
